 Robert Pattinson Wins Bond Role as Henry Cavill Joins Netflix Spy Film

 Robert Pattinson has secured the role of James Bond in the franchise's next installment, ending speculation over Daniel Craig's successor, while Henry Cavill has missed out on the iconic character and moved into another espionage project with Netflix alongside Kevin Hart. The casting decision places Pattinson under director Denis Villeneuve for the next 007 movie.
 According to Collider's November 20 report, Pattinson prevailed over Nicholas Hoult, Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, and Josh O'Connor. His selection marks a new chapter for the franchise following Craig's five-film tenure, which concluded with No Time to Die in 2021.
 Advertisement 
 Scroll To Continue with Content 
 Meanwhile, Cavill will headline the Netflix spy action-comedy The Serpent and The Snake. The production pairs him with Hart, with both actors playing secret agents working for rival organizations.
 Also Read 
 Robert Pattinson's Bond Film Draws Zendaya and Hunter Schafer 
 The project follows the two agents after they meet in a Lamaze class and discover that their spouses have become friends. Their professional rivalry eventually develops into an unexpected partnership as they navigate dangerous situations and impending fatherhood.
 Director Joseph McG, whose full name is Joseph McGinty Nichol, will oversee the production. Jonathan Tropper, Wendy and Lizzie Molyneux, and Adam and Aaron Nee are credited with writing the screenplay.
 The supporting cast includes Justin Lupe, Aja Naomi King, and Jason Isaacs. Behind-the-scenes footage has shown Cavill filming the production in Budapest, Hungary, although Netflix has not announced a release date.
 Also Read 
 Léa Seydoux Dismisses Speculation Over Next Bond Girl 
 Cavill previously competed for James Bond when the franchise was casting Casino Royale in the 2000s. Director Martin Campbell later praised his audition, explaining that the actor had the physical appearance and acting ability required for the character.
 Campbell described Cavill's performance positively when discussing the original casting process with the Daily Express.
 "He looked great in the audition. His acting was tremendous. And look, if Daniel didn't exist, Henry would have made an excellent Bond.
 Also Read 
 Bezos Reveals Pattinson Casting Process as OConnor Exits Bond Race 
 He looked terrific, he was in great physical shape… very handsome, very chiselled. He just looked a little young at that time back then," said Campbell.
 Cavill also addressed his prospects of becoming 007 in an interview with Heat magazine in 2026. At the time, he acknowledged that his age could influence the casting decision while expressing interest in another role within the franchise.
 "What actor wouldn't love to be Bond? But at 42, I'd probably be considered a bit old to start now. I would love to be a Bond villain, though. If it was the right character, I think that would be fascinating to explore," said Cavill.
 Also Read 
 Heartland Tops Netflix Film Chart With 7.3 Million Views 
 His earlier comments emerged when speculation centered on younger candidates. However, Pattinson's eventual selection demonstrated that the casting process ultimately considered actors beyond the younger age group initially discussed.
 Before the official decision, Cavill remained a popular choice among Bond fans. His previous espionage performances included Napoleon Solo in The Man from U.N.C.L.E. (2015), August Walker in Mission: Impossible – Fallout (2018), and the title character in Argylle (2024).
 Following reports that Pattinson had entered the casting process, fans expressed disappointment over Cavill's absence from the leading candidates.
 Also Read

 One fan argued that the discussion about the next Bond should have centered on Cavill from the beginning.
 "All the 'next James Bond' talk shouldn't have even started because it should have been Henry Cavill's gig," one fan wrote on X.
 Another reaction characterized the missed opportunity as a major casting mistake.
 Also Read 
 Netflix Releases Guarding Stars Christmas Romance 
 "Henry Cavill as Bond was RIGHT THERE. What a generational fumble," another fan wrote.
 Support for Cavill continued, with another social media user questioning why the actor had not received the role.
 "Henry Cavill should be James Bond. It shouldn't even be up for debate," a fan commented.
 The age difference between the two actors also became part of the discussion among fans.
 "Imagine considering Robert Pattinson (40 years old) for James Bond but rejecting Henry Cavill because he's 'too old' (43). Make it make sense," another user wrote.
 A fifth fan questioned the casting direction and expressed confidence in Cavill's suitability for the franchise.
 "These casting directors are about to destroy James Bond. SMH. Henry Cavill is the only actor who can embody 007 for the next generation," the fan wrote.
 Separately, entertainment industry blind-item account Enty published an unverified claim suggesting that Cavill had been preparing for a possible opportunity to play Bond. The account linked his physical transformation and commercial activities to an alleged effort to strengthen his position in the casting race.
 "The sudden rebrand of the failed superhero actor, from a watch brand deal to a very noticeable physical transformation, was due to his efforts to be a frontrunner in the Bond race, even though he wasn't in the top five," Enty wrote.
 The account also suggested that Cavill's partner believed securing a major franchise project with Amazon would improve his chances. These claims were not independently confirmed.
 Cavill's career has included several commercial disappointments, despite his international recognition from Superman and The Witcher. His other projects have delivered mixed box office results, while Mission: Impossible – Fallout featured him in a supporting role.
 His departure from The Witcher and the subsequent uncertainty surrounding his return as Superman also affected his career trajectory. The upcoming Highlander reboot represents another major project in his filmography, while The Serpent and The Snake gives him a leading role in Netflix's espionage genre.
 Although Pattinson now leads the next James Bond film, Cavill's latest production reunites him with the spy-action genre without placing him in the 007 franchise. Netflix has yet to confirm the release date for The Serpent and The Snake.
